line: Jung's statements on the animus: the name, the woman's contrasexual figure and the way it speaks, and its place as a mediator.

sections.title: The name and the figure
sections.line: CW9ii ¶26–28: why Jung called the projection-making factor in women the animus, and how it shows itself in argument.

quotes.quote: This results in a considerable psychological difference between men and women, and accordingly I have called the projection-making factor in women the animus, which means mind or spirit.
The animus corresponds to the paternal Logos just as the anima corresponds to the maternal Eros.
As the animus is partial to argument, he can best be seen at work in disputes where both parties know they are right.

sections.title: A mediator, and not to be integrated
sections.line: CW9ii ¶28 and ¶40–41: the animus as psychopomp, and why anima and animus themselves cannot be integrated.

quotes.quote: Thus the animus is a psychopomp, a mediator between the conscious and the unconscious and a personification of the latter.
Though the effects of anima and animus can be made conscious, they themselves are factors transcending consciousness and beyond the reach of perception and volition.
Here we meet the animus of a woman and the anima of a man, two corresponding archetypes whose autonomy and unconsciousness explain the stubbornness of their projections.
